metadata.title: Finite generation conjectures for cohomology over finite fields

nodes.name: Bass' conjecture
nodes.statement: Bass conjectured that for a regular scheme $X$ of finite type over the integers, the higher algebraic $K$-groups are finitely generated \cite{bassln342}.
nodes.statement_short: Higher algebraic $K$-groups of a regular scheme of finite type over $\Z$ are finitely generated.
assumptions: for a regular scheme $X$ of finite type over the integers
conclusions: the higher algebraic $K$-groups are finitely generated

nodes.name: Weil-etale cohomology $H^i_W(X,\Z(n))$
nodes.statement: LIchtenbaum's Weil-etale cohomology $H^i_W(X,\Z(n))$ is defined as the cohomology of $R\Gamma_GR\Gamma_\et(\bar X,\Z(n))$, where $G$ is the Weil-group of the finite field.
nodes.statement_short: Cohomology of $R\Gamma_G R\Gamma_\et(\bar X,\Z(n))$ for $G$ the Weil group of $\F_q$.

nodes.name: Frobenius cohomology $H^i_F(X,\Z(n))$
nodes.statement: The purpose of this article is to relate the two finite generaton conjectures with the help of an intermediate cohomology theory $H^i_F(X,\Z(n))$, which we call Frobenius cohomology. It is defined as the cohomology of $R\Gamma_G\Z(n)(\bar X)$, where $\Z(n)$ is Bloch's cycle complex shifted appropriately.
nodes.statement_short: An intermediate theory between motivic and Weil-etale cohomology, the cohomology of $R\Gamma_G\Z(n)(\bar X)$.
differentia: It is defined as the cohomology of $R\Gamma_G\Z(n)(\bar X)$, where $\Z(n)$ is Bloch's cycle complex shifted appropriately.

nodes.name: Comparison diagram of motivic, Frobenius, Kato and Weil-etale cohomology
nodes.statement: \begin{equation}\begin{CD} @>>>H^i_\Nis(X,\Z(n)) @>\alpha >>H^i_F(X,\Z(n)) @>\beta>> H^{i-1}_K(X,\Z(n)) @>\gamma>>\\ @EEE @Vf VV @Vg VV @VhVV \\ @>>> H^i_\et(X,\Z(n)) @>>> H^i_W(X,\Z(n)) @>>> H^{i-1}_\Nis(X,\Q(n))@>>> \end{CD}\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Two exact rows linked by $f,g,h$, comparing the motivic/Frobenius/Kato row with the etale/Weil-etale row.

nodes.name: Kato cohomology $H^i_K(X,\Z(n))$
nodes.statement: with groups $H^i_K(X,\Z(n))=H^i(\Z(n)(\bar X)_G)$ called Kato cohomology. They are a generalization of the integral version of Kato homology \cite{kato} (which is the case $n=\dim X$) defined in \cite{ichkato}.
nodes.statement_short: The cohomology of the coinvariants $\Z(n)(\bar X)_G$, generalizing integral Kato homology.

nodes.name: Finite generation of the upper row
nodes.statement: We conjecture all groups in the upper row of \eqref{less} to be finitely generated, and believe they form interesting invariants of $X$.
nodes.statement_short: All groups of the motivic/Frobenius/Kato row of the comparison diagram are finitely generated.
conclusions: all groups in the upper row of \eqref{less} to be finitely generated

nodes.name: Kato cohomology under Parshin's conjecture
nodes.statement: For example, $H^{2n}_K(X,\Z(n))=CH^n(\bar X)_G$, and under Parshin's conjecture, the groups $H^i_K(X,\Z(n))$ vanish for $i\leq n$ and are torsion for $i\not= 2n$.
nodes.statement_short: $H^{2n}_K(X,\Z(n))=CH^n(\bar X)_G$, and under Parshin $H^i_K$ vanishes for $i\leq n$ and is torsion off $i=2n$.
conclusions: $H^{2n}_K(X,\Z(n))=CH^n(\bar X)_G$
the groups $H^i_K(X,\Z(n))$ vanish for $i\leq n$ and are torsion for $i\not= 2n$

nodes.name: The first interesting example $H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$
nodes.statement: The first interesting example $H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$ consists of those elements in the cokernel of the integral cycle map $CH^2(X)\to H^4_\et(X,\Z(2))$ which are in the image over the algebraic closure, or in classical language those elements in the unramified cohomology group $H^3_{nr}(X,\Q/\Z(2))$ which vanish in $H^3_{nr}(\bar X,\Q/\Z(2))$.
nodes.statement_short: $H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$ is the part of unramified cohomology that dies over the algebraic closure.

nodes.name: Pirutka's $2$-torsion element
nodes.statement: Pirutka \cite{pirutka} used an idea of Colliot-Th\'el\`ene to construct an element in $H^3_{nr}(X,\Z/2)$ for a geometrically rational surface (in all but finitely many characteristics), providing a $2$-torsion element in $H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$.
nodes.statement_short: A geometrically rational surface carries a nonzero $2$-torsion class in $H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$.

nodes.name: Generality of the constructions
nodes.statement: Since the above theories exist for any scheme of finite type over a finite field, we define them in this generality and later specialize to smooth projective $X$.

nodes.name: Standing setup: schemes over $\F_q$ and the Weil group
nodes.statement: We consider separated schemes of finite type over a finite field $\F_q$ of characteristic $p$, and $n\geq 0$ (the case $n<0$ can be reduced to this case using the homotopy formula). Let $\varphi$ be the geometric Frobenius, and $G=\langle \varphi\rangle$ be the Weil group of $\F_q$.
nodes.statement_short: Throughout: separated finite-type $\F_q$-schemes, $n\geq 0$, $\varphi$ geometric Frobenius, $G=\langle\varphi\rangle$.

nodes.name: Bloch's cycle complex $\Z^c(n)$
nodes.statement: Let $\Z^c(n)$ be the cycle complex defined by Bloch shifted by $2n$, so that $$H_i(\Z^c(n)(X)) = CH_n(X,i-2n).$$ This agrees with motivic cohomology $H^{2d-i}_\Nis(X,\Z(d-n))$ for smooth $X$ of pure dimension $d$ by \cite{voevodsky}.
nodes.statement_short: Bloch's cycle complex shifted by $2n$, computing higher Chow groups $CH_n(X,i-2n)$.
nodes.genus: the cycle complex defined by Bloch shifted by $2n$

nodes.name: $H_i^c$, Frobenius homology $H_i^F$ and Kato homology $H_i^K$
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be an abelian group. \begin{enumerate} \item We define $H_i^c(X,A(n))$ to be $H_i(\Z^c(n)(X)\otimes A)$. \item We define Frobenius homology $H_i^F(X,A(n))$ to be the homology of the double complex $$ \Z^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A \xrightarrow{\varphi-1} \Z^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A.$$ Here $\varphi$ acts covariantly in $\bar X$ on cycles on $\bar X\times \Delta^i$; the left and right hand complexes sit in homological degrees $1$ and $0$, respectively. \item The Kato homology $H_i^K(X,A(n))$ is defined to be the homology of the complex of coinvariants $\big(\Z^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)_G$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Defines $H^c_i$ from $\Z^c(n)(X)\otimes A$, $H^F_i$ as the homology of the $\varphi-1$ double complex, and $H^K_i$ from the coinvariants.
differentia: to be the homology of the double complex $$ \Z^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A \xrightarrow{\varphi-1} \Z^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A.$$

nodes.name: Vanishing range and low-degree identification of $H^c,H^F,H^K$
nodes.statement: The groups $H_i^c(X,A(n))$, $H_i^F(X,A(n))$ and $H_i^K(X,A(n))$ vanish for $i<2n$. We have $H_{2n}^c(X,A(n))\cong CH_n(X)\otimes A$ and $$H_{2n}^K(X,A(n))\cong H_{2n}^F(X,A(n)) \cong \big( CH_n(\bar X)\otimes A\big)_G.$$ For all $i$, there are short exact sequences \begin{equation} 0\to H_i^c(\bar X,A(n))_G\to H_i^F(X,A(n))\to H_{i-1}^c(\bar X,A(n))^G \to 0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: All three theories vanish below degree $2n$, agree with (co)invariants of $CH_n$ in degree $2n$, and $H^F$ sits in a short exact sequence.
conclusions: The groups $H_i^c(X,A(n))$, $H_i^F(X,A(n))$ and $H_i^K(X,A(n))$ vanish for $i<2n$.
We have $H_{2n}^c(X,A(n))\cong CH_n(X)\otimes A$ and $$H_{2n}^K(X,A(n))\cong H_{2n}^F(X,A(n)) \cong \big( CH_n(\bar X)\otimes A\big)_G.$$
For all $i$, there are short exact sequences \begin{equation} 0\to H_i^c(\bar X,A(n))_G\to H_i^F(X,A(n))\to H_{i-1}^c(\bar X,A(n))^G \to 0. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Torsion coefficients compute Galois cohomology
nodes.statement: Note that $H_i^F(X,\Z/m(n))$ is isomorphic to $H^{1-i}(Gal(\F_q),\Z^c/m(n)(\bar X))$ because with torsion coefficients, Galois cohomology can be calculated by the complex above.
nodes.statement_short: With torsion coefficients $H^F_i$ is Galois cohomology of $\Z^c/m(n)(\bar X)$.

nodes.name: Long exact sequence relating $H^c$, $H^F$ and $H^K$
nodes.statement: We have an exact sequence \begin{equation} \cdots\to H_i^c(X,A(n)) \to H_{i+1}^F(X,A(n))\to H_{i+1}^K(X,A(n)) \to H_{i-1}^c(X,A(n)) \to \cdots \end{equation} All three theories are covariently functorial for proper maps, contravariantly functorial for quasi-finite flat maps, and have localization long exact sequences.
nodes.statement_short: A long exact sequence links $H^c$, $H^F$ and $H^K$; all three are proper-covariant, quasi-finite-flat-contravariant and localizing.
conclusions: We have an exact sequence \begin{equation} \cdots\to H_i^c(X,A(n)) \to H_{i+1}^F(X,A(n))\to H_{i+1}^K(X,A(n)) \to H_{i-1}^c(X,A(n)) \to \cdots \end{equation}
All three theories are covariently functorial for proper maps, contravariantly functorial for quasi-finite flat maps, and have localization long exact sequences.

nodes.name: Proof of the long exact sequence and functoriality
nodes.statement: This comes from the short exact sequence of double complexes $$\begin{CD} \big( \Z^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)^G@>>> \Z^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A@>>> 0 \\ @VVV @V\varphi-1 VV@VVV \\ 0@>>> \Z^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A @>>> \big(\Z^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)_G \end{CD}$$ and $\Z^c(n)(X)\otimes A\cong \big(\Z^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)^G$. Functoriality and the localization property are well-known for cycle complexes, and this carries over to $\big( \Z^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)_G$ by an easy diagram chase.
nodes.statement_short: Take homology of a short exact sequence of double complexes, then quote known functoriality of cycle complexes.

nodes.name: Short exact sequence of double complexes
nodes.statement: This comes from the short exact sequence of double complexes $$\begin{CD} \big( \Z^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)^G@>>> \Z^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A@>>> 0 \\ @VVV @V\varphi-1 VV@VVV \\ 0@>>> \Z^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A @>>> \big(\Z^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)_G \end{CD}$$ and $\Z^c(n)(X)\otimes A\cong \big(\Z^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)^G$.
nodes.statement_short: Exhibit the short exact sequence of double complexes yielding the long exact sequence.

nodes.name: Functoriality and localization
nodes.statement: Functoriality and the localization property are well-known for cycle complexes, and this carries over to $\big( \Z^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)_G$ by an easy diagram chase.
nodes.statement_short: Transport known functoriality/localization of cycle complexes to the coinvariants by a diagram chase.

nodes.name: Frobenius cohomology of a finitely generated field
nodes.statement: For a finitely generated field $K$ of transcendence degree $d$ over $\F_q$, define $H^i_F(K,A(j))$ to be $\colim H_{2d+1-i}^F(U,A(d-j))$, where $U$ runs through smooth schemes with function field $K$.
nodes.statement_short: $H^i_F(K,A(j))$ is the colimit of $H^F_{2d+1-i}(U,A(d-j))$ over smooth models $U$ of $K$.
differentia: where $U$ runs through smooth schemes with function field $K$

nodes.name: Frobenius descent short exact sequence for fields
nodes.statement: \begin{multline} 0\to H^{s-t-1}_\Nis(K\otimes_{\F_q}\bar \F_q,A(s-n))_G \to H^{s-t}_F(K,A(s-n))\to \\ H^{s-t}_\Nis(K\otimes_{\F_q}\bar \F_q,A(s-n))^G\to 0, \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Coinvariants-invariants short exact sequence computing $H^{s-t}_F(K,A(s-n))$.

nodes.name: Niveau spectral sequences for $H^c$ and $H^F$
nodes.statement: We have functorial spectral sequences \begin{align*} E^1_{s,t}=\bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} H^{s-t}_\Nis(k(x),A(s-n))&\Rightarrow H_{s+t}^c(X,A(n));\\ \bar E^1_{s,t}=\bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} H^{s-t}_F(k(x),A(s-n))&\Rightarrow H_{s+t+1}^F(X,A(n)).\\ \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Niveau filtration gives spectral sequences from field-level motivic (resp. Frobenius) cohomology to $H^c$ (resp. $H^F$).
assumptions: We consider separated schemes of finite type over a finite field $\F_q$ of characteristic $p$, and $n\geq 0$
conclusions: We have functorial spectral sequences \begin{align*} E^1_{s,t}=\bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} H^{s-t}_\Nis(k(x),A(s-n))&\Rightarrow H_{s+t}^c(X,A(n));\\ \bar E^1_{s,t}=\bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} H^{s-t}_F(k(x),A(s-n))&\Rightarrow H_{s+t+1}^F(X,A(n)).\\ \end{align*}

nodes.name: Proof of the niveau spectral sequences
nodes.statement: This follows with the niveau filtration, together with the fact that $$H_{s+t}^c(K,A(n)):= \colim_{U} H_{s+t}^c(U,A(n)) \cong H^{s-t}_\Nis(K,A(s-n))$$ and $H_{s+t+1}^F(K,A(n))\cong H^{s-t}_F(K,A(s-n))$ for a field $K$ of transcendence degree $s$ over the base field.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the niveau filtration plus the field-level identifications of $H^c$ and $H^F$.

nodes.name: Finite generation of $H^c$, $H^F$ and $H^K$ with integral coefficients
nodes.statement: The groups $H_i^c(X,\Z(n))$, $H_{i}^F(X,\Z(n))$ and $H_{i}^K(X,\Z(n))$ are finitely generated for any $i, n$ and $X$.
conclusions: The groups $H_i^c(X,\Z(n))$, $H_{i}^F(X,\Z(n))$ and $H_{i}^K(X,\Z(n))$ are finitely generated for any $i, n$ and $X$.

nodes.name: Reduction to smooth and proper $X$
nodes.statement: By localization, it suffices to consider the case of smooth and proper $X$ (assuming that every finitely generated field over $\F_q$ has a smooth and proper model). This case will be considered in detail below.

nodes.name: Parshin's conjecture $P_n$
nodes.statement: Recall from \cite{ichparshin} Parshin's conjecture $P_n$, stating that $CH_n(X,i)$ is torsion for $i\not=0$ and $X$ smooth and projective.
nodes.statement_short: Higher Chow groups $CH_n(X,i)$ of a smooth projective $X$ are torsion for $i\neq 0$.
conclusions: $CH_n(X,i)$ is torsion for $i\not=0$

nodes.name: Field-level comparison of motivic and Frobenius cohomology under $P_n$
nodes.statement: Assume Conjecture $P_n$. Then $$H^{s-t}_\Nis(k,\Z(s-n))\cong H^{s-t}_F(k,\Z(s-n))$$ for $t\geq n$. For $t=n-1$, the left hand side vanishes, and $H^{s-n+1}_F(k,\Z(s-n))\cong K_{s-n}^M(k\otimes_{\F_q}\bar \F_q)_G$. For $t<n-1$, both sides vanish.
nodes.statement_short: Under Parshin, $H^{s-t}_\Nis(k,\Z(s-n))\cong H^{s-t}_F(k,\Z(s-n))$ for $t\geq n$, with a Milnor $K$-theory term at $t=n-1$.
conclusions: Then $$H^{s-t}_\Nis(k,\Z(s-n))\cong H^{s-t}_F(k,\Z(s-n))$$ for $t\geq n$.
For $t=n-1$, the left hand side vanishes, and $H^{s-n+1}_F(k,\Z(s-n))\cong K_{s-n}^M(k\otimes_{\F_q}\bar \F_q)_G$.
For $t<n-1$, both sides vanish.

nodes.name: Proof of the field-level comparison
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that the second map and the composition $$H^{s-t}_\Nis(k,\Z(s-n))\to H^{s-t}_F(k,\Z(s-n)) \to H^{s-t}_\et(k,\Z(s-n))$$ are isomorphism for $t\geq n$. The total composition is an isomorphism for $t\geq n-1$ by the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures. For the second map, we compare \eqref{frobdescent} to the analog short exact sequence for etale cohomology. By Parshin's conjecture, the groups $H^i_\Nis(k,\Z(s-n))$ are torsion for $i<s-n$, so that Galois cohomology and cohomology of the Weil-group $G$ agree for those groups. The result now follows with the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures by comparing \eqref{frobdescent} with the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence for Galois cohomology (for the finite product of fields $k\otimes_{\F_q}\bar\F_q$).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the second map, use Beilinson-Lichtenbaum for the total composition, then compare descent sequences using Parshin.

nodes.name: Reduce to two maps
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that the second map and the composition $$H^{s-t}_\Nis(k,\Z(s-n))\to H^{s-t}_F(k,\Z(s-n)) \to H^{s-t}_\et(k,\Z(s-n))$$ are isomorphism for $t\geq n$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the claim to the second map and the total composition being isomorphisms.

nodes.name: Total composition via Beilinson-Lichtenbaum
nodes.statement: The total composition is an isomorphism for $t\geq n-1$ by the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures.
nodes.statement_short: The total composition is an isomorphism for $t\geq n-1$ by Beilinson-Lichtenbaum.

nodes.name: Parshin makes Galois and Weil-group cohomology agree
nodes.statement: For the second map, we compare \eqref{frobdescent} to the analog short exact sequence for etale cohomology. By Parshin's conjecture, the groups $H^i_\Nis(k,\Z(s-n))$ are torsion for $i<s-n$, so that Galois cohomology and cohomology of the Weil-group $G$ agree for those groups.
nodes.statement_short: Compare the Frobenius descent sequence with its etale analogue; Parshin forces the relevant groups to be torsion.

nodes.name: Conclude by Hochschild-Serre
nodes.statement: The result now follows with the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures by comparing \eqref{frobdescent} with the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence for Galois cohomology (for the finite product of fields $k\otimes_{\F_q}\bar\F_q$).
nodes.statement_short: Finish by comparing with the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence for the product of fields.

nodes.name: Kato complex $KC_n(X)$ of weight $n$
nodes.statement: We define the Kato complex $KC_n(X)$ of weight $n$ to be the complex $$ \bigoplus_{X_{(n)}} \Z \gets \bigoplus_{X_{(n+1)}} (k(x)\otimes_{\F_q}\bar\F_q)^\times_G \gets \cdots\gets \bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} K_{s-n}^M(k(x)\otimes_{\F_q}\bar\F_q)_G \gets\cdots,$$ with the summand indexed by $X_{(s)}$ in degree $s-n$. The differentials are induced by boundary maps of higher Chow groups of discrete valuation rings.
nodes.statement_short: A complex of Milnor $K$-theory coinvariants indexed by points of $X$, with boundary maps from higher Chow groups of DVRs.
differentia: with the summand indexed by $X_{(s)}$ in degree $s-n$
The differentials are induced by boundary maps of higher Chow groups of discrete valuation rings.

nodes.name: Kato homology computed by the Kato complex
nodes.statement: Assuming conjecture $P_n$, we have $$H_i^K(X,\Z(n))\cong H_{i-2n}(KC_n(X)).$$ In particular, $H_i^K(X,\Z(n))$ vanishes unless $2n\leq i\leq n+d$.
nodes.statement_short: Under $P_n$, $H^K_i(X,\Z(n))$ is the homology of $KC_n(X)$ and vanishes outside $2n\leq i\leq n+d$.
conclusions: we have $$H_i^K(X,\Z(n))\cong H_{i-2n}(KC_n(X)).$$
In particular, $H_i^K(X,\Z(n))$ vanishes unless $2n\leq i\leq n+d$.

nodes.name: Proof that Kato homology is the homology of $KC_n(X)$
nodes.statement: Compare the spectral sequences of Proposition \ref{ssprop} and use Proposition \ref{pupl}.
nodes.statement_short: Compare the niveau spectral sequences and insert the field-level comparison.

nodes.name: Why finite coefficients
nodes.statement: Considering finite coefficients allows us to remove the hypothesis on Parshin's conjecture and to compare to etale homology.

nodes.name: Mod-$m$ long exact sequence
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} \cdots\to H_i^c(X,\Z/m(n)) \stackrel{\alpha}{\to} H_{i+1}^F(X,\Z/m(n)) \stackrel{\beta}{\to} H_{i+1}^K(X,\Z/m(n))\to \cdots \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The $H^c$-$H^F$-$H^K$ long exact sequence with $\Z/m$ coefficients.

nodes.name: Finiteness with finite coefficients
nodes.statement: All terms in the \eqref{hommodm} are finite for all $i, n, X$.
conclusions: All terms in the \eqref{hommodm} are finite for all $i, n, X$.

nodes.name: Structure map $f:X\to \F_q$
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to \F_q$ be the structure map.

nodes.name: Borel-Moore etale homology $H^\et_i(X,\Z/m(n))$
nodes.statement: For $p\not|m$ we define $H^\et_i(X,\Z/m(n))$ as the (Borel-Moore) etale homology $H^{-i}(X_\et,Rf^!\mu_m^{\otimes -n})= H^{-i}(Gal(\F_q),R\Gamma_\et(\bar X, Rf^!\mu_m^{\otimes -n}))$.
nodes.statement_short: Etale Borel-Moore homology defined by $Rf^!\mu_m^{\otimes -n}$, equivalently Galois cohomology of its $\bar X$-sections.

nodes.name: Vanishing of etale homology below degree $-1$
nodes.statement: The groups $H^\et_i(X,\Z/m(n))$ vanish for $i<-1$.
assumptions: Since $Gal(\F_q)$ has cohomological dimension $1$ and $Rf^!\mu_m^{\otimes -n}$ is concentrated in negative degrees
conclusions: The groups $H^\et_i(X,\Z/m(n))$ vanish for $i<-1$.

nodes.name: Duality: $Rf^!\Z/m \cong \Z^c/m(0)$
nodes.statement: We have $Rf^!\Z/m \cong \Z^c/m(0)$ for any $m$. In particular $H^\et_i(X,\Z/m(n))$ agrees with the $-i$th etale hypercohomology of $\Z^c/m(n)$ if $p\not|m$ and $n\leq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: The dualizing complex is the mod-$m$ cycle complex, identifying etale homology with etale hypercohomology of $\Z^c/m(n)$.
conclusions: We have $Rf^!\Z/m \cong \Z^c/m(0)$ for any $m$.
In particular $H^\et_i(X,\Z/m(n))$ agrees with the $-i$th etale hypercohomology of $\Z^c/m(n)$ if $p\not|m$ and $n\leq 0$.

nodes.name: Finiteness conjecture for $n=0$
nodes.statement: Let $n=0$. Then Conjecture \ref{finitehom} holds for $p\not| m$, and for any $m$ under resolution of singularities.
nodes.statement_short: For $n=0$ the finiteness conjecture holds away from $p$, and for all $m$ under resolution of singularities.
conclusions: Then Conjecture \ref{finitehom} holds for $p\not| m$, and for any $m$ under resolution of singularities.

nodes.name: Proof of the $n=0$ finiteness theorem
nodes.statement: If $n=0$, then $\gamma$ is an isomorphism by \cite{ichduality}, hence Frobenius homology is finite. But by Jannsen-Kerz-Saito \cite{kerzsaito}, Kato homology is finite. If $m=p^r$, then Kato homology is finite under resolution of singularities. To show finiteness of Frobenius homology, one reduces by the usual devissage to the case that $X$ is smooth and proper of dimension $d$. In this case, $\gamma$ is an isomorphic to the finite group $H^{d-i}_\et(X,\nu^{d}_r)$ by Theorem \ref{dduuaall} and the isomorphism $\Z^c/p^r(0) \cong \nu^d_r[d]$.
nodes.statement_short: Split on the coefficient: away from $p$ use duality plus Jannsen-Kerz-Saito; for $m=p^r$ devissage to smooth proper $X$.

nodes.name: Case $p\not|m$
nodes.statement: If $n=0$, then $\gamma$ is an isomorphism by \cite{ichduality}, hence Frobenius homology is finite. But by Jannsen-Kerz-Saito \cite{kerzsaito}, Kato homology is finite.
nodes.statement_short: For $n=0$, $\gamma$ is an isomorphism so $H^F$ is finite, and Kato homology is finite by Jannsen-Kerz-Saito.

nodes.name: Case $m=p^r$
nodes.statement: If $m=p^r$, then Kato homology is finite under resolution of singularities. To show finiteness of Frobenius homology, one reduces by the usual devissage to the case that $X$ is smooth and proper of dimension $d$. In this case, $\gamma$ is an isomorphic to the finite group $H^{d-i}_\et(X,\nu^{d}_r)$ by Theorem \ref{dduuaall} and the isomorphism $\Z^c/p^r(0) \cong \nu^d_r[d]$.
nodes.statement_short: For $p$-power coefficients reduce by devissage to smooth proper $X$ and identify $\gamma$ with a finite etale group.

nodes.name: The comparison map $\gamma$ to etale homology
nodes.statement: This construction induces a a map $$ \Z^c/m(n)(\bar X) \to R\Gamma_\et(\bar X, \Z^c/m(n))\to R\Gamma_\et(\bar X,Rf^!\mu^{\otimes -n}),$$ hence $$\gamma: H_{i+1}^F(X,\Z/m(n))\to H_i^\et(X,\Z/m(n))$$ by taking the cone of $\varphi-1$.
nodes.statement_short: Cap-product with the Bott element induces $\gamma:H^F_{i+1}(X,\Z/m(n))\to H^\et_i(X,\Z/m(n))$.

nodes.name: Failure of the comparison for $n>0$
nodes.statement: This map is in general not an isomorphism for $n>0$; for example, the left hand side vanishes for $n>\dim X$, but the right hand side is periodic in $n$.

nodes.name: Niveau spectral sequence for etale homology
nodes.statement: For $p\not| m$ we have a spectral sequence \begin{equation} \tilde E^1_{s,t}=\bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} H^{s-t}_\et(k(x),\mu_m^{\otimes s-n}) \Rightarrow H_{s+t}^\et(X,\Z/m(n)) \end{equation} The $\tilde E^1$-terms lie in short exact sequences \begin{multline} 0\to H^{s-t-1}_\et(k(x)\otimes_{\F_q}\bar \F_q,\mu_m^{\otimes s-n})_G \to H^{s-t}_\et(k(x),\mu_m^{\otimes s-n})\to \\ H^{s-t}_\et(k(x)\otimes_{\F_q}\bar \F_q,\mu_m^{\otimes s-n})^G\to 0. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: A niveau spectral sequence converging to $H^\et_{s+t}(X,\Z/m(n))$, whose $E^1$-terms sit in Galois descent sequences.
conclusions: we have a spectral sequence \begin{equation} \tilde E^1_{s,t}=\bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} H^{s-t}_\et(k(x),\mu_m^{\otimes s-n}) \Rightarrow H_{s+t}^\et(X,\Z/m(n)) \end{equation}

The $\tilde E^1$-terms lie in short exact sequences \begin{multline} 0\to H^{s-t-1}_\et(k(x)\otimes_{\F_q}\bar \F_q,\mu_m^{\otimes s-n})_G \to H^{s-t}_\et(k(x),\mu_m^{\otimes s-n})\to \\ H^{s-t}_\et(k(x)\otimes_{\F_q}\bar \F_q,\mu_m^{\otimes s-n})^G\to 0. \end{multline}

nodes.name: Field-level comparison with finite coefficients
nodes.statement: For $k$ a field of transcendence degree $s$ over $\F_q$ and $p\not|m$, $$H^{s-t}_\Nis(k,\Z/m(s-n))\cong H^{s-t}_F(k,\Z/m(s-n)) \cong H^{s-t}_\et(k,\mu_m^{\otimes s-n}) $$ for $t\geq n$. The left term vanishes for $t<n$, the middle term vanishes for $t<n-1$ and $$H^{s-n+1}_F(k,\Z/m(s-n))\cong H^{s-n}_\Nis(k\otimes_{\F_q}\bar \F_q,\Z/m(s-n))_G \subseteq H^{s-n+1}_\et(k,\mu_m^{\otimes s-n})$$ The right term vanishes for $t<-1$.
nodes.statement_short: For fields and $p\not|m$, motivic, Frobenius and etale cohomology agree for $t\geq n$, with prescribed vanishing ranges.
assumptions: For $k$ a field of transcendence degree $s$ over $\F_q$ and $p\not|m$
conclusions: $$H^{s-t}_\Nis(k,\Z/m(s-n))\cong H^{s-t}_F(k,\Z/m(s-n)) \cong H^{s-t}_\et(k,\mu_m^{\otimes s-n}) $$ for $t\geq n$.

The left term vanishes for $t<n$, the middle term vanishes for $t<n-1$ and $$H^{s-n+1}_F(k,\Z/m(s-n))\cong H^{s-n}_\Nis(k\otimes_{\F_q}\bar \F_q,\Z/m(s-n))_G \subseteq H^{s-n+1}_\et(k,\mu_m^{\otimes s-n})$$
The right term vanishes for $t<-1$.

nodes.name: Proof of the field-level comparison with finite coefficients
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that the maps $$H^{s-t}_\Nis(k,\Z/m(s-n))\to H^{s-t}_F(k,\Z(s-n)) \to H^{s-t}_\et(k,\Z/m(s-n))$$ are isomorphism for $t\geq n$. The total composition is an isomorphism by the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures. Comparing the sequences \eqref{frobdescent} and \eqref{galoismodm}, it follows that the second map is an isomorphism by the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures for the finite product of fields $k\otimes_{\F_q}\bar\F_q$.
nodes.statement_short: Beilinson-Lichtenbaum gives the total composition; comparing the two descent sequences gives the second map.

nodes.name: Reduce to the two maps
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that the maps $$H^{s-t}_\Nis(k,\Z/m(s-n))\to H^{s-t}_F(k,\Z(s-n)) \to H^{s-t}_\et(k,\Z/m(s-n))$$ are isomorphism for $t\geq n$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to showing the displayed maps are isomorphisms for $t\geq n$.

nodes.name: Total composition by Beilinson-Lichtenbaum
nodes.statement: The total composition is an isomorphism by the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures.
nodes.statement_short: The total composition is an isomorphism by Beilinson-Lichtenbaum.

nodes.name: Compare descent sequences
nodes.statement: Comparing the sequences \eqref{frobdescent} and \eqref{galoismodm}, it follows that the second map is an isomorphism by the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures for the finite product of fields $k\otimes_{\F_q}\bar\F_q$.
nodes.statement_short: Compare the Frobenius and Galois descent sequences to get the second map.

nodes.name: Mod-$m$ Kato complex $KC_n/m(X)$
nodes.statement: We define $KC_n/m(X)$ to be the complex \begin{multline} \bigoplus_{X_{(n)}} \Z/m \gets \bigoplus_{X_{(n+1)}} H^1_\et(k(x)\otimes_{\F_q}\bar\F_q,\Z/m(1))_G \gets \cdots \\ \gets \bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} H^{s-n}_\et(k(x)\otimes_{\F_q}\bar\F_q,\Z/m(s-n))_G \gets\cdots, \end{multline} with the summand indexed by $X_{(s)}$ in degree $s-n$.
nodes.statement_short: The mod-$m$ analogue of the Kato complex, built from etale cohomology coinvariants of residue fields.
differentia: with the summand indexed by $X_{(s)}$ in degree $s-n$

nodes.name: Mod-$m$ Kato homology via $KC_n/m(X)$
nodes.statement: We have $$H_i^K(X,\Z/m(n))\cong H_{i-2n}(KC_n/m(X)),$$ and theses groups vanish unless $2n\leq i\leq n+d$.
conclusions: We have $$H_i^K(X,\Z/m(n))\cong H_{i-2n}(KC_n/m(X)),$$
and theses groups vanish unless $2n\leq i\leq n+d$.

nodes.name: Smooth and proper $X$ over $\F_q$
nodes.statement: In this section we assume that $X$ is smooth and proper over $\F_q$, and discuss what other conjectures (like Parshin's conjecture) imply for the cohomology groups defined above.

nodes.name: Bloch's cycle complex indexed by codimension $\Z(n)$
nodes.statement: Let $\Z(n)$ be Bloch's higher cycle complex indexed by codimension, so that $\Z(n)(X)^i=z^n(X,2n-i)$ and $H^{i}_{Zar}(X,\Z(n))=CH_{d-n}(X,2n-i)$ is motivic cohomology for smooth $X$ of pure dimension $d$.
nodes.statement_short: The codimension-indexed cycle complex whose Zariski hypercohomology is motivic cohomology.
nodes.genus: Bloch's higher cycle complex indexed by codimension

nodes.name: Cohomological notation for $H^i_F$ and $H^i_K$
nodes.statement: If $X$ is smooth of pure dimension $d$, we set \begin{align} H^i_F(X,A(n))&=H_{2d+1-i}^F(X,A(d-n))\\ H^i_K(X,A(n))&=H_{2d-i}^K(X,A(d-n)). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Reindexes Frobenius and Kato homology as cohomology via Poincare-type duality shifts.

nodes.name: Cohomological form of the vanishing and exact sequences
nodes.statement: The groups $H^i_F(X,A(n))$ vanish for $i>2n+1$, and in general there are short exact sequences $$ 0\to H^{i-1}_\Nis(\bar X,A(n))_G\to H^i_F(X,A(n))\to H^i_\Nis(\bar X,A(n))^G \to 0.$$ The groups $H^i_K(X,A(n))$ vanish for $i>2n$, and $$H^{2n}_K(X,A(n))\cong H^{2n+1}_F(X,A(n)) \cong \big(CH^n(\bar X)\otimes A\big)_G.$$
nodes.statement_short: $H^i_F$ vanishes above $2n+1$ and sits in a descent sequence; $H^i_K$ vanishes above $2n$ with $H^{2n}_K\cong (CH^n(\bar X)\otimes A)_G$.
assumptions: In this section we assume that $X$ is smooth and proper over $\F_q$
conclusions: The groups $H^i_F(X,A(n))$ vanish for $i>2n+1$, and in general there are short exact sequences $$ 0\to H^{i-1}_\Nis(\bar X,A(n))_G\to H^i_F(X,A(n))\to H^i_\Nis(\bar X,A(n))^G \to 0.$$
The groups $H^i_K(X,A(n))$ vanish for $i>2n$, and $$H^{2n}_K(X,A(n))\cong H^{2n+1}_F(X,A(n)) \cong \big(CH^n(\bar X)\otimes A\big)_G.$$

nodes.name: Commutative comparison diagram with exact rows
nodes.statement: We have a commutative diagram with exact rows \begin{equation}\begin{CD} @>>>{\bf H^i_\Nis(X,\Z(n))} @>\alpha >>{\bf H^i_F(X,\Z(n))} @>\beta>> {\bf H^{i-1}_K(X,\Z(n))} @>\gamma>>\\ @EEE @Vf VV @Vg VV @VhVV \\ @>>> H^i_\et(X,\Z(n)) @>>> {\bf H^i_W(X,\Z(n)) }@>>> H^{i-1}_\Nis(X,\Q(n))@>>> \end{CD}\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The motivic/Frobenius/Kato row maps to the etale/Weil-etale row in a commutative diagram with exact rows.
assumptions: In this section we assume that $X$ is smooth and proper over $\F_q$
conclusions: We have a commutative diagram with exact rows \begin{equation}\begin{CD} @>>>{\bf H^i_\Nis(X,\Z(n))} @>\alpha >>{\bf H^i_F(X,\Z(n))} @>\beta>> {\bf H^{i-1}_K(X,\Z(n))} @>\gamma>>\\ @EEE @Vf VV @Vg VV @VhVV \\ @>>> H^i_\et(X,\Z(n)) @>>> {\bf H^i_W(X,\Z(n)) }@>>> H^{i-1}_\Nis(X,\Q(n))@>>> \end{CD}\end{equation}

nodes.name: Proof of the comparison diagram
nodes.statement: The upper row is exact by Proposition \ref{prop1}, and the lower row is the exact sequence relating etale cohomology to Weil-etale cohomology \cite{ichweilI}. The maps $f$ and $g$ are induced by the change of topology from the Zariski to the etale site.
nodes.statement_short: Exactness of the two rows comes from the earlier proposition and Weil-etale cohomology; $f,g$ are change-of-topology maps.

nodes.name: Exactness of the two rows
nodes.statement: The upper row is exact by Proposition \ref{prop1}, and the lower row is the exact sequence relating etale cohomology to Weil-etale cohomology \cite{ichweilI}.
nodes.statement_short: Upper row exact by the earlier proposition, lower row by the Weil-etale exact sequence.

nodes.name: Identify the vertical maps
nodes.statement: The maps $f$ and $g$ are induced by the change of topology from the Zariski to the etale site.
nodes.statement_short: The vertical maps $f$ and $g$ come from the Zariski-to-etale change of topology.

nodes.name: Vertical maps are rational isomorphisms
nodes.statement: The vertical maps are isomorphisms after tensoring with $\Q$, because motivic cohomology and etale hypercohomology of the motivic complex agree with rational coefficients.

nodes.name: Finite generation of the bold face terms
nodes.statement: The bold face terms are finitely generated for all $i,n$ and $X$.
conclusions: The bold face terms are finitely generated for all $i,n$ and $X$.

nodes.name: Relation to Bass', Tate's and Beilinson's conjectures
nodes.statement: Finite generation of $H^i_\Nis(X,\Z(n))$ is a generalization of Bass' conjecture, and finite generation of $H^i_W(X,\Z(n))$ is equivalent to Tate's and Beilinson's conjecture.

nodes.name: Lichtenbaum's conjecture on etale motivic cohomology
nodes.statement: The group $H^i_\et(X,\Z(n))$ is finite for all $i\not=2n,2n+1$, finitely generated for all $i=2n$, and of cofinite type for $i=2n+2$.
nodes.statement_short: $H^i_\et(X,\Z(n))$ is finite off $i=2n,2n+1$, finitely generated at $i=2n$, cofinite type at $i=2n+2$.
conclusions: The group $H^i_\et(X,\Z(n))$ is finite for all $i\not=2n,2n+1$
finitely generated for all $i=2n$
of cofinite type for $i=2n+2$

nodes.name: Low-degree behaviour of $h$
nodes.statement: The map $h:H^i_K(X,\Z(n))\to H^i_\Nis(X,\Q(n))$ is bijective for $i<n$ and injective for $i=n$.
assumptions: In this section we assume that $X$ is smooth and proper over $\F_q$
conclusions: The map $h:H^i_K(X,\Z(n))\to H^i_\Nis(X,\Q(n))$ is bijective for $i<n$ and injective for $i=n$.

nodes.name: Proof of the low-degree behaviour of $h$
nodes.statement: By the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures, both the map $f$ as well as the map $g$ are isomorphism for $i\leq n+1$ and injective for $i=n+2$.
nodes.statement_short: Beilinson-Lichtenbaum makes $f$ and $g$ isomorphisms up to degree $n+1$ and injective at $n+2$.

nodes.name: The case $n=0$
nodes.statement: Conjecture \ref{maincohom} holds for $n=0$. In fact we have $H^i_F(X,\Z)\cong H^i_W(X,\Z)\cong \Z$ for $i=0,1$, $H^0_K(X,\Z)\cong H^0_\Nis(X,\Z)\cong \Z$, and all other homology groups vanish.
nodes.statement_short: For $n=0$ all the groups are $\Z$ in degrees $0,1$ (resp. $0$) and vanish otherwise, so the conjecture holds.
conclusions: Conjecture \ref{maincohom} holds for $n=0$.
In fact we have $H^i_F(X,\Z)\cong H^i_W(X,\Z)\cong \Z$ for $i=0,1$, $H^0_K(X,\Z)\cong H^0_\Nis(X,\Z)\cong \Z$, and all other homology groups vanish.

nodes.name: The case $n=1$
nodes.statement: Let $n=1$. a) For $i=1$, the four left groups in \eqref{maind} are isomorphic to ${\mathcal O}_X(X)^\times$, and for $i=2$, they are isomorphic to $\Pic(X)$. b) The groups $H^i_K(X,\Z(1))$ vanish for $i\not=2$, and $H^2_K(X,\Z(1))\cong \NS(\bar X)_G$. c) For $i=3$, \begin{align*} H^3_\Nis(X,\Z(1))&=0\\ H^3_\et(X,\Z(1))&\cong \Br(X)\\ H^3_F(X,\Z(1))&\cong \NS(\bar X)_G, \end{align*} and $H^3_W(X,\Z(1))$ is an extension of $Br(\bar X)^G$ by $NS(\bar X)_G$. d) All groups in \eqref{maind} are finitely generated, except possibly $H^3_\et(X,\Z(1))\cong \Br(X)$ and $H^3_W(X,\Z(1))$, whose finiteness is equivalent to Tate's conjecture for divisors.
nodes.statement_short: For $n=1$ the groups are units, $\Pic$, $\NS(\bar X)_G$ and $\Br(X)$, all finitely generated except where Tate's conjecture for divisors is needed.
conclusions: a) For $i=1$, the four left groups in \eqref{maind} are isomorphic to ${\mathcal O}_X(X)^\times$, and for $i=2$, they are isomorphic to $\Pic(X)$.
b) The groups $H^i_K(X,\Z(1))$ vanish for $i\not=2$, and $H^2_K(X,\Z(1))\cong \NS(\bar X)_G$.

c) For $i=3$, \begin{align*} H^3_\Nis(X,\Z(1))&=0\\ H^3_\et(X,\Z(1))&\cong \Br(X)\\ H^3_F(X,\Z(1))&\cong \NS(\bar X)_G, \end{align*} and $H^3_W(X,\Z(1))$ is an extension of $Br(\bar X)^G$ by $NS(\bar X)_G$.
d) All groups in \eqref{maind} are finitely generated, except possibly $H^3_\et(X,\Z(1))\cong \Br(X)$ and $H^3_W(X,\Z(1))$, whose finiteness is equivalent to Tate's conjecture for divisors.

nodes.name: Proof of the case $n=1$
nodes.statement: This follows from $\Z(1)\cong {\mathbb G}_m[-1]$, Lemma \ref{plm} and $(\Pic^0 \bar X)_G =0$.
nodes.statement_short: Use $\Z(1)\cong \G_m[-1]$, the cohomological vanishing lemma, and $(\Pic^0\bar X)_G=0$.

nodes.name: The case $n=2$ under Parshin's conjecture
nodes.statement: Now consider the case $n=2$. According to Parshin's conjecture and Lemma \ref{lowdegree}, the groups $H^i_K(X,\Z(2))$ vanish for $i\leq 2$, and $H^4_K(X,\Z(2))\cong CH^2(\bar X)_G$.
nodes.statement_short: Parshin plus the low-degree lemma make $H^i_K(X,\Z(2))$ vanish for $i\leq2$ and identify $H^4_K$ with $CH^2(\bar X)_G$.
assumptions: According to Parshin's conjecture and Lemma \ref{lowdegree}
conclusions: the groups $H^i_K(X,\Z(2))$ vanish for $i\leq 2$
$H^4_K(X,\Z(2))\cong CH^2(\bar X)_G$

nodes.name: The map $\tau$ to unramified cohomology
nodes.statement: To describe the remaining group, let $\epsilon:X_{\et}\to X_{\Zar}$ be the canonical map of sites, and $\tau$ the composition of the boundary map in the lower row of \eqref{maind} with the composition $$H^4_\et(X,\Z(2))\to H^0(X,R^4\epsilon_*\Z(2))\cong H^0(X,R^3\epsilon_*\Q/\Z(2)) =H^3_{nr}(X,\Q/\Z(2)).$$ The last term is known under the name unramified cohomology.
nodes.statement_short: $\tau$ composes the boundary map of the Weil-etale row with the edge map onto $H^3_{nr}(X,\Q/\Z(2))$.
nodes.genus: the composition of the boundary map in the lower row of \eqref{maind}

nodes.name: Torsion in $H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$ via unramified cohomology
nodes.statement: The group ${}_\tor H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$ is isomorphic to the cohomology of the sequence $$ H^2_\Nis(X,\Q(2))\stackrel{\tau}{\to} H^3_{nr}(X,\Q/\Z(2))\to H^3_{nr}(\bar X,\Q/\Z(2))^G.$$
nodes.statement_short: ${}_\tor H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$ is the cohomology of $H^2_\Nis(X,\Q(2))\to H^3_{nr}(X,\Q/\Z(2))\to H^3_{nr}(\bar X,\Q/\Z(2))^G$.
assumptions: In this section we assume that $X$ is smooth and proper over $\F_q$
conclusions: The group ${}_\tor H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$ is isomorphic to the cohomology of the sequence $$ H^2_\Nis(X,\Q(2))\stackrel{\tau}{\to} H^3_{nr}(X,\Q/\Z(2))\to H^3_{nr}(\bar X,\Q/\Z(2))^G.$$

nodes.name: Proof of the unramified description of $H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$
nodes.statement: The first statement follows from a diagram chase in \eqref{maind}, noting that due to the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjecture the maps $f$ and $g$ are injective, $\coker f=H^0(X,R^4\epsilon_*\Z(2))$ and $$\coker g= \coker\big( H^4_\Nis(\bar X,\Z(2))^G\to H^4_\et(\bar X,\Z(2))^G\big) \subseteq H^0(\bar X,R^4\epsilon_*\Z(2))^G.$$
nodes.statement_short: Diagram chase in the comparison diagram, computing $\coker f$ and $\coker g$ via Beilinson-Lichtenbaum injectivity.

nodes.name: Exact sequence for $H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$ under Parshin
nodes.statement: Under Parshin's conjecture there is an exact sequence $$0\to H^3_K(X,\Z(2))\to H^3_{nr}(X,\Q/\Z(2))\to H^3_{nr}(\bar X,\Q,\Z(2))^G .$$ Thus ${}_\tor H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$ consists of those elements in the cokernel of the integral cyle map, whose pull back to the algebraic closure $H^4_\et(\bar X,\Z(2))$ lie in the image of the cycle map $CH^n(\bar X)\to H^{2n}_\et(\bar X,\Z(n))$.
nodes.statement_short: $H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$ injects into unramified cohomology and measures classes dying over $\bar\F_q$.
conclusions: there is an exact sequence $$0\to H^3_K(X,\Z(2))\to H^3_{nr}(X,\Q/\Z(2))\to H^3_{nr}(\bar X,\Q,\Z(2))^G .$$

Thus ${}_\tor H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$ consists of those elements in the cokernel of the integral cyle map, whose pull back to the algebraic closure $H^4_\et(\bar X,\Z(2))$ lie in the image of the cycle map $CH^n(\bar X)\to H^{2n}_\et(\bar X,\Z(n))$.

nodes.name: Proof of the exact sequence for $H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$
nodes.statement: Under Parshin's conjecture, $H^3_k(X,\Z(2))$ is torsion. Furthermore, $\coker f$ is the obstruction to the integral Tate conjecture, and $\coker g$ is the cokernel of the map $CH^2(\bar X)^G\to H^4_\et(\bar X,\Z(2))^G$.
nodes.statement_short: Parshin makes the group torsion; then identify $\coker f$ and $\coker g$ with obstructions to the integral Tate conjecture.

nodes.name: Torsion under Parshin
nodes.statement: Under Parshin's conjecture, $H^3_k(X,\Z(2))$ is torsion.
nodes.statement_short: Parshin's conjecture makes $H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$ torsion.

nodes.name: Identify the cokernels
nodes.statement: Furthermore, $\coker f$ is the obstruction to the integral Tate conjecture, and $\coker g$ is the cokernel of the map $CH^2(\bar X)^G\to H^4_\et(\bar X,\Z(2))^G$.
nodes.statement_short: Recognize $\coker f$ as the integral Tate obstruction and $\coker g$ as the cokernel of the cycle map over $\bar\F_q$.

nodes.name: Geometrically rational $X$
nodes.statement: If $X$ is geometrically rational, then there are isomorphisms $H^3_{nr}(X,\Q/\Z(2))\cong H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$.
conclusions: there are isomorphisms $H^3_{nr}(X,\Q/\Z(2))\cong H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$

nodes.name: Proof for geometrically rational $X$
nodes.statement: For rational $Z$ over a field $k$, we have $H^3_{nr}(Z,\Q/\Z(2))=H^3_\et(k,\Q/\Z(2))$, and $H^2_\Nis(Z,\Q(2))\cong H^0(Z,{\mathcal H}^2(\Q(2)))\cong H^2_\Nis(k,\Q(2)) $ by \cite[2.1.9]{cothe}, and for $k$ the algebraic closure of a finite field these groups vanish.
nodes.statement_short: Unramified cohomology of a rational variety reduces to the base field, whose groups vanish over $\bar\F_q$.

nodes.name: Pirutka's element on a fivefold
nodes.statement: Pirutka \cite{pirutka} constructed an element in $H^3_{nr}(X,\Z/2)$ for $X$ a geometrically birational variety of dimension $5$, giving a non-trivial $2$-torsion element in $H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$.
nodes.statement_short: A geometrically birational fivefold with a nonzero $2$-torsion class in $H^3_K(X,\Z(2))$.

nodes.name: The case $n=\dim X$
nodes.statement: If $n=\dim X$, then Conjecture \ref{maincohom} is equivalent to conjecture $P_0$. In this case, $H^i_K(X,\Z(n))=0$ for $i\not=2n$, and $H^{2n}_K(X,\Z(n))\cong \Z^{\pi_0(X)}$.
nodes.statement_short: For $n=\dim X$ the finite-generation conjecture is equivalent to $P_0$, and $H^{2n}_K(X,\Z(n))\cong \Z^{\pi_0(X)}$.
conclusions: Conjecture \ref{maincohom} is equivalent to conjecture $P_0$
In this case, $H^i_K(X,\Z(n))=0$ for $i\not=2n$, and $H^{2n}_K(X,\Z(n))\cong \Z^{\pi_0(X)}$.

nodes.name: Cohomological Parshin conjecture $P^n$
nodes.statement: The cohomological Parshin conjecture $P^n$ of \cite{parshinneu} states that $H^i_\Nis(X,\Q(n))=0$ for smooth and proper $X$ and $i\not=2n$.
nodes.statement_short: $H^i_\Nis(X,\Q(n))=0$ for smooth proper $X$ and $i\neq 2n$.

nodes.name: Consequences of Parshin's conjecture for $H^i_K$
nodes.statement: This is equivalent to isomorphisms $H^i_\et(X,\Z(n)) \cong H^i_W(X,\Z(n))$ for $i\leq 2n$, and injectivity in degree $2n+1$ by \cite{ichweilI}. By Lemma \ref{lowdegree}, Parshin's conjecture implies that the groups $H^i_K(X,\Z(n))$ vanish for $i\leq n$ if $n>0$, and that they torsion for $i\leq 2n$.
nodes.statement_short: Parshin identifies etale with Weil-etale cohomology up to degree $2n$ and forces $H^i_K$ to vanish for $i\leq n$ and be torsion for $i\leq 2n$.
conclusions: This is equivalent to isomorphisms $H^i_\et(X,\Z(n)) \cong H^i_W(X,\Z(n))$ for $i\leq 2n$, and injectivity in degree $2n+1$ by \cite{ichweilI}.
the groups $H^i_K(X,\Z(n))$ vanish for $i\leq n$ if $n>0$, and that they torsion for $i\leq 2n$.

nodes.name: Comparison diagram in degrees $i<2n$
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} @>>> H^i_\Nis(X,\Z(n)) @>>> H^i_F(X,\Z(n)) @>>> H^{i-1}_K(X,\Z(n))\to \cdots \\ @III @VVV @VVV \\ @EEE H^i_\et(X,\Z(n)) @= H^i_W(X,\Z(n)) \end{CD}\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Under Parshin the diagram collapses so that etale and Weil-etale cohomology agree for $i<2n$.

nodes.name: Comparison diagram in degree $2n$
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} H^{2n-2}_K(X,\Z(n))@>>> CH^n(X) @>\alpha >> H^{2n}_F(X,\Z(n)) @>>> H^{2n-1}_K(X,\Z(n))\to 0\\ @III @Vf VV @Vg VV \\ @EEE H^{2n}_\et(X,\Z(n)) @= H^{2n}_W(X,\Z(n)) \end{CD}\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: In degree $2n$ the cycle class map $CH^n(X)\to H^{2n}_F$ sits in a four-term sequence over the etale/Weil-etale comparison.

nodes.name: Kernel-cokernel sequence for $f$ and $g$

nodes.name: Reduction to the map over the algebraic closure
nodes.statement: As we saw, the map $H^i_\Nis(X,\Z(n))\to H^i_F(X,\Z(n))$ is controlled by $H^i_K(X,\Z(n))$. The maps $H^i_F(X,\Z(n))\to H^i_W(X,\Z(n))$ and $H^i_F(X,\Z/m(n))\to H^i_\et(X,\Z/m(n))$ arise by taking Galois descent on the maps $$ H^i_\Nis(\bar X,\Z(n)) \to H^i_\et(\bar X,\Z(n)).$$ It is thus important to get some ideas of the properties of this map. Since it is an isomorphism rationally, we focus on finite coefficients.

nodes.name: Finiteness of $H^i_\Nis(\bar X,\Z/m(n))$
nodes.statement: The question is if $H^i_\Nis(\bar X,\Z/m(n))$ is finite. nodes.name: Equivalence of Lichtenbaum's conjecture and finite generation of $H^i_W$
nodes.statement: Fix an integer $n$ and a scheme $X$, and consider the following statements: \begin{enumerate} \item Lichtenbaum's conjecture \ref{lichtconj}. \item The groups $H^i_W(X,\Z(n))$ are finitely generated. \item Parshin's conjecture. \end{enumerate} Then $a)\Leftrightarrow b) \Rightarrow c)$.
nodes.statement_short: Lichtenbaum's conjecture and finite generation of Weil-etale cohomology are equivalent, and both imply Parshin's conjecture.
assumptions: Fix an integer $n$ and a scheme $X$, and consider the following statements: \begin{enumerate} \item Lichtenbaum's conjecture \ref{lichtconj}. \item The groups $H^i_W(X,\Z(n))$ are finitely generated. \item Parshin's conjecture. \end{enumerate}
conclusions: Then $a)\Leftrightarrow b) \Rightarrow c)$.

nodes.name: Proof of the equivalence
nodes.statement: $a)\Rightarrow c)$ This follows because $H^i_\et(X,\Q(n))\cong H^i_\Nis(X,\Q(n))$, and the former vanishes for $i\not=2n$ by hypothesis. To show the equivalence of a) and b) we can assume Parshin's conjecture, and consider the exact sequence of \cite{ichweilI} $$ \cdots \to H^i_\et(X,\Z(n))\to H^i_W(X,\Z(n))\to H^{i-1}_\Nis(X,\Q(n))\to \cdots.$$ Then a) and b) imply each other for $i\leq 2n$ and $i>2n+2$, and we are left with \begin{multline*} 0\to H^{2n+1}_\et(X,\Z(n))\to H^{2n+1}_W(X,\Z(n))\to H^{2n}_\Nis(X,\Q(n))\\ \to H^{2n+2}_\et(X,\Z(n))\to H^{2n+2}_W(X,\Z(n))\to 0 . \end{multline*} By the Weil-conjectures and counting coranks one sees that the corank $C$ of $H^{2n+2}_\et(X,\Z(n))\cong H^{2n+1}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(n))$ and of $H^{2n}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(n))$ agree. a) $\Rightarrow$ b): Finiteness of $H^{2n+1}_\et(X,\Z(n))$ implies that $C$ agrees with the dimension of $H^{2n}_\et(X,\Q(n))$, and since $H^{2n+2}_\et(X,\Z(n))$ is torsion, $H^{2n+1}_W(X,\Z(n))/\tor$ must be a lattice of the same rank. Moreover $H^{2n}_\Nis(X,\Q(n))$ surjects onto the divisible part of $H^{2n+2}_\et(X,\Z(n))$, hence $H^{2n+2}_W(X,\Z(n))$ is finite. b) $\Rightarrow$ a) We see that $H^{2n+1}_\et(X,\Z(n))$ is finite, because $H^{2n+1}_W(X,\Q(n))\cong H^{2n}(X,\Q(n))$ \cite{ichweilI}. For the same reason, $H^{2n+2}_\et(X,\Z(n))$ is an extension of the finite group $H^{2n+2}_W(X,\Z(n))$ and a torsion divisible group of finite corank.
nodes.statement_short: Derive Parshin from a), then compare coranks in the Weil-etale exact sequence to get a) and b) from each other.

nodes.name: a) implies c)
nodes.statement: $a)\Rightarrow c)$ This follows because $H^i_\et(X,\Q(n))\cong H^i_\Nis(X,\Q(n))$, and the former vanishes for $i\not=2n$ by hypothesis.
nodes.statement_short: Lichtenbaum's conjecture forces rational motivic cohomology to vanish off $i=2n$.

nodes.name: Set up the corank count
nodes.statement: To show the equivalence of a) and b) we can assume Parshin's conjecture, and consider the exact sequence of \cite{ichweilI} $$ \cdots \to H^i_\et(X,\Z(n))\to H^i_W(X,\Z(n))\to H^{i-1}_\Nis(X,\Q(n))\to \cdots.$$ Then a) and b) imply each other for $i\leq 2n$ and $i>2n+2$, and we are left with \begin{multline*} 0\to H^{2n+1}_\et(X,\Z(n))\to H^{2n+1}_W(X,\Z(n))\to H^{2n}_\Nis(X,\Q(n))\\ \to H^{2n+2}_\et(X,\Z(n))\to H^{2n+2}_W(X,\Z(n))\to 0 . \end{multline*} By the Weil-conjectures and counting coranks one sees that the corank $C$ of $H^{2n+2}_\et(X,\Z(n))\cong H^{2n+1}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(n))$ and of $H^{2n}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(n))$ agree.
nodes.statement_short: Assume Parshin, reduce to the five-term sequence and compare coranks via the Weil conjectures.

nodes.name: a) implies b)
nodes.statement: a) $\Rightarrow$ b): Finiteness of $H^{2n+1}_\et(X,\Z(n))$ implies that $C$ agrees with the dimension of $H^{2n}_\et(X,\Q(n))$, and since $H^{2n+2}_\et(X,\Z(n))$ is torsion, $H^{2n+1}_W(X,\Z(n))/\tor$ must be a lattice of the same rank. Moreover $H^{2n}_\Nis(X,\Q(n))$ surjects onto the divisible part of $H^{2n+2}_\et(X,\Z(n))$, hence $H^{2n+2}_W(X,\Z(n))$ is finite.
nodes.statement_short: Finiteness at $2n+1$ pins the rank of $H^{2n+1}_W/\tor$ and forces $H^{2n+2}_W$ finite.

nodes.name: b) implies a)
nodes.statement: b) $\Rightarrow$ a) We see that $H^{2n+1}_\et(X,\Z(n))$ is finite, because $H^{2n+1}_W(X,\Q(n))\cong H^{2n}(X,\Q(n))$ \cite{ichweilI}. For the same reason, $H^{2n+2}_\et(X,\Z(n))$ is an extension of the finite group $H^{2n+2}_W(X,\Z(n))$ and a torsion divisible group of finite corank.
nodes.statement_short: Finite generation of Weil-etale cohomology gives finiteness of $H^{2n+1}_\et$ and the structure of $H^{2n+2}_\et$.

nodes.name: Factorization of the $l$-adic cycle map
nodes.statement: the $l$-adic cycle map can be factored as follows: $$ c:H^i_\Nis(X,\Z(n))\otimes\Z_l \stackrel{u}{\to} H^i_\et(X,\Z(n))\otimes\Z_l \stackrel{v}{\to} H^i_\et(X,\Z(n))^{\wedge l} \stackrel{w}{\hookrightarrow} H^i_\et(X,\hat\Z_l(n)).$$
nodes.statement_short: $c$ factors as change of topology $u$, $l$-adic completion $v$ and inclusion $w$ into continuous etale cohomology.

nodes.name: Surjectivity of the completion map $v$
nodes.statement: The completion map $v$ is surjective.

conclusions: The completion map $v$ is surjective.

nodes.name: Proof that $v$ is surjective
nodes.statement: The $\Z_l$-module $H^i_\et(X,\Z(n))^{\wedge l}\subseteq H^i_\et(X,\hat\Z_l(n))$ is finitely generated and the cokernel of $v$ is $l$-divsible by \cite[(4.2)]{jannsencont}, hence must be trivial.
nodes.statement_short: The target is finitely generated over $\Z_l$ while $\coker v$ is $l$-divisible, so it vanishes.

nodes.name: Kernel-cokernel sequence for the cycle map factorization
nodes.statement: We have an exact sequence \begin{multline*} 0\to \ker u\to \ker c\to {\rm div}\; H^i_\et(X,\Z(n))\otimes\Z_l \\ \to \coker u\to \coker c\to T_lH^{i+1}(X_\et,\Z(n))\to 0. \end{multline*} The groups $\ker u$ and $\coker u$ are torsion.
nodes.statement_short: A six-term sequence relates $\ker/\coker$ of $u$ and $c$ through divisible elements and the Tate module.

The groups $\ker u$ and $\coker u$ are torsion.

nodes.name: Proof of the kernel-cokernel sequence
nodes.statement: This is the kernel-cokernel sequence of the composition $c= (wv)\circ u$. The kernel of $wv$ is the kernel of $v$, which is the group of divisible elements of $H^i_\et(X,\Z(n))\otimes \Z_l$. The cokernel of $wv$ is the Tate module $T_lH^{i+1}(X,\Z(n))$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the kernel-cokernel sequence to $c=(wv)\circ u$ and identify $\ker wv$ and $\coker wv$.

nodes.name: Identify the kernel

nodes.name: Kernel and cokernel of $u$ under Lichtenbaum's conjecture
nodes.statement: Under Conjecture \ref{lichtconj}, the kernel and cokernel of $u$ are equal to the kernel and cokernel of the cycle map, respectively.

conclusions: the kernel and cokernel of $u$ are equal to the kernel and cokernel of the cycle map, respectively

nodes.name: Rational surjectivity and Tate's conjecture
nodes.statement: The cycle map $CH^n(X)\otimes \Z_l\to H^{2n}_\et(X,\hat\Z_l(n))$ is rationally surjective if and only if $T_lH^{i+1}(X,\Z(n))$ vanishes, hence Tate's conjecture is equivalent to $\Div H^{2n+1}_\et(X,\Z(n))$ torsion free.

nodes.name: Rational injectivity and Beilinson's conjecture
nodes.statement: It is rationally injective (Beilinson's conjecture) if and only if $\div H^{2n}_\et(X,\Z(n))$ is torsion.
nodes.statement_short: Rational injectivity is equivalent to $\div H^{2n}_\et(X,\Z(n))$ being torsion.

nodes.name: Short exact sequence for $\coker u$
nodes.statement: Considering the diagram $$\begin{CD} H^{2n-1}_\Nis(X,\Q/\Z(n))@>inj>> H^{2n}_\Nis(X,\Z(n))@>>> H^{2n}_\Nis(X,\Q(n)) @>surj>> H^{2n}_\Nis(X,\Q/\Z(n))\\ @VrVV @VuVV @| @VsVV \\ H^{2n-1}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(n))@>inj>> H^{2n}_\et(X,\Z(n))@>>> H^{2n}_\et(X,\Q(n)) @>>> H^{2n}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(n)), \end{CD}$$ we obtain a short exact sequence $0\to \coker r\to \coker u\to \ker s\to 0$, and all three groups are conjecturally finite.
nodes.statement_short: $\coker u$ is an extension of $\ker s$ by $\coker r$, all three conjecturally finite.
conclusions: we obtain a short exact sequence $0\to \coker r\to \coker u\to \ker s\to 0$, and all three groups are conjecturally finite.

nodes.name: Proof of the weight vanishing lemma
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{polk1}, $\tilde E^1_{s,t}$ vanishes for $t<-1$: The first statement follows because $$H^{s}_\et(k\otimes_{\F_q}\bar \F_q,\Q/\Z'(s-1)) \cong \big( K_s^M(k\otimes_{\F_q}\bar \F_q)\otimes\Q/\Z(-1)\big)$$ can be written as $M\otimes \Q/\Z(-1)$ for a discrete $G$-module $M$. Hence the coinvariants vanish \cite{schneider}. For the second statement note that $$H^{s+1}_\et(k(x),\Q/\Z'(s-1))\cong H^{s}_\et(k(x)\otimes_{\F_q}\bar \F_q,\Q/\Z'(s-1))_\varphi$$ for cohomological dimension reasons.

nodes.name: The complex $KC_1^{F\et}(X)$ and its homology $C_i(X)$
nodes.statement: Consequently, the difference between $H_i^F(X,\Q/\Z(1))$ and $H_i^\et(X,\Q/\Z^c(1))$ is measured by the homology $C_i(X)$ of the complex $KC_1^{F\et}(X)$ which is the difference between $\bar E_{s,0}$ and $\tilde E_{s,0}$ (we put the term indexed by $X_{(s)}$ in degree $s$). \begin{multline*} \bigoplus_{X_{(0)}} \Q/\Z(-1)^\varphi \gets \bigoplus_{X_{(1)}} H^1_\et(k(x)\otimes_{\F_q}\bar\F_q,\Q/\Z(0))^\varphi \gets \cdots \\ \gets \bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} H^{s}_\et(k(x)\otimes_{\F_q}\bar\F_q,\Q/\Z(s-1))^\varphi \gets\cdots, \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: $C_i(X)$ is the homology of the complex measuring the gap between Frobenius and etale homology at $n=1$.
differentia: which is the difference between $\bar E_{s,0}$ and $\tilde E_{s,0}$

nodes.name: Exact sequences relating $H^F$, etale homology and $C_i(X)$
nodes.statement: There are exact sequences $$ \cdots \to H_3^F(X,\Q/\Z(1)) \to H_2^\et(X,\Q/\Z^c(1))\to\\ C_2(X)\to 0$$ and $$ 0\to H_2^F(X,\Q/\Z(1))\to H_1^\et(X,\Q/\Z^c(1))\to C_1(X) \to 0$$ and an isomorphism $H_0^\et(X,\Q/\Z^c(1))\cong C_0(X)$. The second sequence is isomorphic to $$ 0\to (CH_1(\bar X)\otimes \Q/\Z)_\varphi\to H_1^\et(X,\Q/\Z^c(1)) \to H_0^\et(\bar X,\Q/\Z^c(1))^\varphi \to 0.$$
nodes.statement_short: Short exact sequences express $C_1,C_2$ as cokernels of $H^F\to H^\et$, with $H_0^\et\cong C_0$.
conclusions: There are exact sequences $$ \cdots \to H_3^F(X,\Q/\Z(1)) \to H_2^\et(X,\Q/\Z^c(1))\to\\ C_2(X)\to 0$$ and $$ 0\to H_2^F(X,\Q/\Z(1))\to H_1^\et(X,\Q/\Z^c(1))\to C_1(X) \to 0$$
and an isomorphism $H_0^\et(X,\Q/\Z^c(1))\cong C_0(X)$.

nodes.name: Finiteness of all $C_i(X)$
nodes.statement: All groups $C_i(X)$ are finite.
conclusions: All groups $C_i(X)$ are finite.

nodes.name: Cohomological form of the end of the $C_i$ sequence
nodes.statement: In cohomological notation, the end of the sequence is $$ H^{2d-2}_F(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))\to H^{2d-2}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))\to C_2(X)\to 0$$ $$ 0\to H^{2d-1}_F(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))\to H^{2d-1}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1)) \to C_1(X)\to 0,$$ with $H^{2d-1}_F(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))\cong (CH_1(\bar X)\otimes\Q/\Z)_\varphi$ divisible and $C_1(X)= H^{2d-1}_\et(\bar X,\Q/\Z(d-1))^\varphi$ finite. Next $H^{2d}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))\cong C_0(X)$ is finite, and $H^{2d+1}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))=H^{2d}_\et(\bar X,\Q/\Z(d-1))_\varphi=0$ by the Weil-conjectures.
nodes.statement_short: In cohomological notation $C_1(X)$ is finite, $C_0(X)$ is finite and the next etale group vanishes by the Weil conjectures.
conclusions: In cohomological notation, the end of the sequence is $$ H^{2d-2}_F(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))\to H^{2d-2}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))\to C_2(X)\to 0$$ $$ 0\to H^{2d-1}_F(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))\to H^{2d-1}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1)) \to C_1(X)\to 0,$$

with $H^{2d-1}_F(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))\cong (CH_1(\bar X)\otimes\Q/\Z)_\varphi$ divisible and $C_1(X)= H^{2d-1}_\et(\bar X,\Q/\Z(d-1))^\varphi$ finite. Next $H^{2d}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))\cong C_0(X)$ is finite, and $H^{2d+1}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))=H^{2d}_\et(\bar X,\Q/\Z(d-1))_\varphi=0$ by the Weil-conjectures.

nodes.name: Finiteness of $C_2(X)$ is Tate's conjecture
nodes.statement: The finiteness of $C_2(X)$ is Tate's conjecture.

nodes.name: The sequence for a surface
nodes.statement: For a surface, the non-trivial part of the sequence takes the form $$ 0\to H^2_F(X,\Q/\Z(1)) \to H^2_\et(X,\Q/\Z(1))\to \Br(X)\to 0 .$$
nodes.statement_short: For a surface the sequence reads $0\to H^2_F(X,\Q/\Z(1))\to H^2_\et(X,\Q/\Z(1))\to \Br(X)\to 0$.

nodes.name: The complex $KC_1^{M\et}(X)$ and its cohomology $B_i(X)$
nodes.statement: Finally, the total difference between $H_i^c(X,\Q/\Z(1))$ and $H_i^\et(X,\Q/\Z^c(1))$ is measured by the cohomology $B_i(X)$ of the extension $KC_1^{M\et}(X)$ of $KC_1^{F\et}(X)$ by $KC_1(X)$ (where the term indexed by $X_{(s)}$ is located in degree $s$): \begin{multline*} \bigoplus_{X_{(0)}} H^0_\et(k(x),\Q/\Z(-1)) \gets \bigoplus_{X_{(1)}} H^1_\et(k(x),\Q/\Z(0))\gets \cdots \\ \gets \bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} H^{s}_\et(k(x),\Q/\Z(s-1)) \gets\cdots. \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: $B_i(X)$ measures the total gap between $H^c_i$ and etale homology with $\Q/\Z(1)$-coefficients.
nodes.genus: the cohomology $B_i(X)$ of the extension $KC_1^{M\et}(X)$ of $KC_1^{F\et}(X)$ by $KC_1(X)$

nodes.name: Exact sequences for $B_i(X)$
nodes.statement: There is an exact sequence \begin{multline*} \cdots\to H_3^c(X,\Q/\Z(1)) \to H_3^\et(X,\Q/\Z^c(1))\to B_3(X)\to \\ H_2^c(X,\Q/\Z(1))\to H_2^\et(X,\Q/\Z^c(1))\to B_2(X) \to 0 \end{multline*} and isomorphisms $H_i^\et(X,\Q/\Z^c(1))\cong B_i(X)$ for $i=0,1$. For cohomology this translates into \begin{multline*} \cdots\to H^{2d-3}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))\to H^{2d-3}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))\to B_3(X)\to \\ CH^{d-1}(X)\otimes\Q/\Z\to H^{2d-2}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))\to B_2(X) \to 0 \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: A long exact sequence links $H^c_i$, etale homology and $B_i(X)$, in homological and cohomological notation.
conclusions: There is an exact sequence \begin{multline*} \cdots\to H_3^c(X,\Q/\Z(1)) \to H_3^\et(X,\Q/\Z^c(1))\to B_3(X)\to \\ H_2^c(X,\Q/\Z(1))\to H_2^\et(X,\Q/\Z^c(1))\to B_2(X) \to 0 \end{multline*}

nodes.name: Structure of the groups $B_i(X)$
nodes.statement: a) Parshin's conjecture and Bass' conjecture imply finiteness of $B_i(X)$ for $i>3$. b) $B_3(X)=0$. c) $B_2(X)\cong H^{2d-1}_\et(X,\Z(d-1))$ is conjecturally finite, and Tate's conjecture is equivalent to its Tate module vanishing. It does not vanish in general, beause for $d=2$ it is the Brauer group of a surface. d) $B_1(X) \cong H^{2d-1}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))$ is of cofinite type. Under Tate's conjecture, its corank equals $\dim CH_1(X)_\Q$. e) $B_0(X)\cong H^{2d}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))\cong \F_q^\times$.
nodes.statement_short: Finiteness of $B_i$ for $i>3$ under Parshin and Bass; $B_3=0$, $B_2$ is a Brauer-type group, $B_1$ cofinite type, $B_0\cong \F_q^\times$.
assumptions: For the remainder of this section, we ignore $p$-torsion groups.
conclusions: a) Parshin's conjecture and Bass' conjecture imply finiteness of $B_i(X)$ for $i>3$.

c) $B_2(X)\cong H^{2d-1}_\et(X,\Z(d-1))$ is conjecturally finite, and Tate's conjecture is equivalent to its Tate module vanishing. It does not vanish in general, beause for $d=2$ it is the Brauer group of a surface.
d) $B_1(X) \cong H^{2d-1}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))$ is of cofinite type. Under Tate's conjecture, its corank equals $\dim CH_1(X)_\Q$.
e) $B_0(X)\cong H^{2d}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))\cong \F_q^\times$.

nodes.name: Proof of the structure of $B_i(X)$
nodes.statement: First note that $H^i_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))$ is finite for $i\not= 2d-2, 2d-1$. a) Follows from the long exact sequence and the finiteness of the etale cohomology groups. b) Is Schoen's result on the surjectivity of the integral cycle map. c) Is a conjecture of Lichtenbaum. d) $B_1(X)$ differs from $H^{2d-2}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))_\varphi$ by a finite group. e) By the affine Lefschetz theorem, $$H^{2d}_\et(\bar X,\Q/\Z(d-1))^\varphi \cong H^0_\et(\bar \F_q,\Q/\Z(-1))^\varphi\cong \F_q^\times$$ on the one hand, and $H^{2d-1}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))_\varphi$ vanishes for weight reasons on the other hand.
nodes.statement_short: Item-by-item: finiteness of etale cohomology, Schoen's surjectivity, Lichtenbaum's conjecture, and the affine Lefschetz theorem.

nodes.name: Finiteness of the etale groups
nodes.statement: First note that $H^i_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))$ is finite for $i\not= 2d-2, 2d-1$.
nodes.statement_short: Record that $H^i_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))$ is finite outside two degrees.

nodes.name: Part a)
nodes.statement: a) Follows from the long exact sequence and the finiteness of the etale cohomology groups.
nodes.statement_short: Finiteness for $i>3$ from the long exact sequence.

nodes.name: Part b)
nodes.statement: b) Is Schoen's result on the surjectivity of the integral cycle map.
nodes.statement_short: Vanishing of $B_3$ is Schoen's surjectivity result.

nodes.name: Part c)
nodes.statement: c) Is a conjecture of Lichtenbaum.
nodes.statement_short: The conjectural finiteness of $B_2$ is Lichtenbaum's conjecture.

nodes.name: Part d)
nodes.statement: d) $B_1(X)$ differs from $H^{2d-2}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))_\varphi$ by a finite group.
nodes.statement_short: $B_1$ differs from the coinvariants by a finite group.

nodes.name: Part e)
nodes.statement: e) By the affine Lefschetz theorem, $$H^{2d}_\et(\bar X,\Q/\Z(d-1))^\varphi \cong H^0_\et(\bar \F_q,\Q/\Z(-1))^\varphi\cong \F_q^\times$$ on the one hand, and $H^{2d-1}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))_\varphi$ vanishes for weight reasons on the other hand.
nodes.statement_short: Affine Lefschetz plus a weight argument identify $B_0$ with $\F_q^\times$.

nodes.name: Sequence relating $B_i$, $C_i$ and Kato homology
nodes.statement: There is also a sequence $$\cdots \to H^K_{i+1}(X,\Q/\Z)\to B_i(X) \to C_i(X)\to H^K_{i}(X,\Q/\Z) \to \cdots\to B_1(X)\to C_1(X)\to 0.$$ and $B_0(X)\cong C_0(X)$.
nodes.statement_short: A long exact sequence connects Kato homology, $B_i(X)$ and $C_i(X)$, with $B_0\cong C_0$.
conclusions: There is also a sequence $$\cdots \to H^K_{i+1}(X,\Q/\Z)\to B_i(X) \to C_i(X)\to H^K_{i}(X,\Q/\Z) \to \cdots\to B_1(X)\to C_1(X)\to 0.$$ and $B_0(X)\cong C_0(X)$.

nodes.name: Finiteness of all the groups except $B_1$ and $H_2^K$
nodes.statement: We wonder if all groups are finite, except $B_1(X)$ and $H_2^K(X,\Q/\Z)$.

nodes.name: $X$ over the algebraic closure, $p$-torsion ignored
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be over the algebraic closure of a finite field; we still ignore $p$-torsion groups.

nodes.name: The complex $KC_1^{sep}(X)$ and its cohomology $T_i(X)$
nodes.statement: The difference between $H_i^\Nis(X,\Q/\Z^c(1))$ and $H_i^\et(X,\Q/\Z^c(1))$ is measured by the cohomology $T_i(X)$ of the complex $KC_1^{sep}(X)$ (where the term indexed by $X_{(s)}$ is located in degree $s$): \begin{multline*} \bigoplus_{X_{(0)}} H^0_\et(k(x),\Q/\Z(-1)) \gets \bigoplus_{X_{(1)}} H^1_\et(k(x),\Q/\Z(0))\gets \cdots \\ \gets \bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} H^{s}_\et(k(x),\Q/\Z(s-1)) \gets\cdots. \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: $T_i(X)$ measures the gap between Nisnevich and etale homology of $X$ over an algebraically closed field.

nodes.name: Exact sequences for $T_i(X)$
nodes.statement: So there is an exact sequence \begin{multline*} \cdots\to H_3^c(X,\Q/\Z(1)) \to H_3^\et(X,\Q/\Z^c(1))\to T_3(X)\to \\ H_2^c(X,\Q/\Z(1))\to H_2^\et(X,\Q/\Z^c(1))\to T_2(X) \to 0 \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: A long exact sequence links $H^c_i$, etale homology and $T_i(X)$, with $H^\et_i\cong T_i$ for $i=0,1$.
conclusions: So there is an exact sequence \begin{multline*} \cdots\to H_3^c(X,\Q/\Z(1)) \to H_3^\et(X,\Q/\Z^c(1))\to T_3(X)\to \\ H_2^c(X,\Q/\Z(1))\to H_2^\et(X,\Q/\Z^c(1))\to T_2(X) \to 0 \end{multline*}

nodes.name: Structure of the groups $T_i(X)$
nodes.statement: a) We don't know anything for $T_i(X)$ for $i>2$. b) $T_2(X)\cong H^{2d-1}_\et(X,\Z(d-1))$ is the cokernel of the cycle map over the algebraic closure (i.e. those cycles which are "transcentental"). It is not finite in general, beause for $d=2$ it is the Brauer group of a surface. c) $T_1(X) \cong H^{2d-1}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))\cong Alb_X(\bar k)(-1)$ is torsion divisible, Pontrjagin dual to $H^1_\et(X,\hat \Z(1))$. d) $T_0(X)\cong H^{2d}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))\cong \Q/\Z(-1)$.
nodes.statement_short: $T_2$ is the cokernel of the cycle map over $\bar k$ (Brauer group for surfaces), $T_1\cong Alb_X(\bar k)(-1)$ and $T_0\cong\Q/\Z(-1)$.
assumptions: Let $X$ be over the algebraic closure of a finite field; we still ignore $p$-torsion groups.
conclusions: a) We don't know anything for $T_i(X)$ for $i>2$.

b) $T_2(X)\cong H^{2d-1}_\et(X,\Z(d-1))$ is the cokernel of the cycle map over the algebraic closure (i.e. those cycles which are "transcentental"). It is not finite in general, beause for $d=2$ it is the Brauer group of a surface.
c) $T_1(X) \cong H^{2d-1}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))\cong Alb_X(\bar k)(-1)$ is torsion divisible, Pontrjagin dual to $H^1_\et(X,\hat \Z(1))$.

nodes.name: Proof of the structure of $T_i(X)$
nodes.statement: Note that $H^i_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))$ is of cofinite type. b) This follows because $H^{2d-1}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d))\cong {}_{tor}CH_0(X)$ and Rojtman's theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Cofinite type of the etale groups, plus Rojtman's theorem for part b).

nodes.name: Cofinite type
nodes.statement: Note that $H^i_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d-1))$ is of cofinite type.
nodes.statement_short: Record that the etale groups are of cofinite type.

nodes.name: Part b) via Rojtman
nodes.statement: b) This follows because $H^{2d-1}_\et(X,\Q/\Z(d))\cong {}_{tor}CH_0(X)$ and Rojtman's theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Identify torsion zero-cycles and apply Rojtman's theorem.

nodes.name: Frobenius descent for the complexes $KC_1^{sep}$
nodes.statement: For any $X$ we have a short exact sequence of complexes $$ 0\to KC_1^{Fet}(X)\to KC_1^{sep}(\bar X) \stackrel{\varphi-1}{\longrightarrow}KC_1^{sep}(\bar X)\to 0$$ and hence a long exact sequence $$\cdots \to C_i(X)\to T_i(\bar X) \stackrel{\varphi -1}{\to} T_i(\bar X)\to C_{i-1}(X)\to \cdots .$$
nodes.statement_short: A $\varphi-1$ short exact sequence of complexes yields a long exact sequence between $C_i(X)$ and $T_i(\bar X)$.
conclusions: we have a short exact sequence of complexes $$ 0\to KC_1^{Fet}(X)\to KC_1^{sep}(\bar X) \stackrel{\varphi-1}{\longrightarrow}KC_1^{sep}(\bar X)\to 0$$
and hence a long exact sequence $$\cdots \to C_i(X)\to T_i(\bar X) \stackrel{\varphi -1}{\to} T_i(\bar X)\to C_{i-1}(X)\to \cdots .$$

nodes.name: Proof of the Frobenius descent sequence
nodes.statement: This follows with Lemma \ref{weights}.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the weight vanishing lemma.

nodes.name: Surface case of the $C_2$-to-$T_0$ sequence
nodes.statement: For a surface, the sequence starting with $C_2(X)$ and ending in $T_0(\bar X)$ takes the form: \begin{multline*} 0\to \Br(X) \to \Br(\bar X)\stackrel{\varphi-1}{\to}\Br(\bar X) \to \\ H^3(X_\et,\Q/\Z(1)) \to CH_0(\bar X)(-1)\stackrel{\varphi-1}{\to} CH_0(\bar X)(-1)\to 0 \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: For a surface the sequence runs from $\Br(X)$ through $\Br(\bar X)$ to $CH_0(\bar X)(-1)$.
